level.title: A1 Beginner Tamil
goals: Understand and produce level-appropriate Tamil in real contexts.
Read target script with consistent romanisation support.
Use respectful, age-friendly language with cultural awareness.

lessons.title: Greetings and Respect
lessons.learn: Learn greetings used across Tamil-speaking communities. Tamil is read left to right. Use நீங்கள் (nīṅkaḷ) with elders and new people; spoken forms may differ from formal written forms.

grammar.title: Respectful identity sentences
grammar.explain: Tamil commonly omits an overt “is” in simple identity sentences. Pronouns and respectful forms carry social meaning.

examples.t: வணக்கம்! நான் கார்த்திக். நீங்கள் எப்படி இருக்கிறீர்கள்?
examples.r: Vaṇakkam! Nāṉ Kārttik. Nīṅkaḷ eppaḍi irukkiṟīrkaḷ?
examples.en: Hello! I'm Karthik. How are you?

examples.t: நான் நன்றாக இருக்கிறேன், நன்றி. நீங்கள் எந்த ஊர்?
examples.r: Nāṉ naṉṟāka irukkiṟēṉ, naṉṟi. Nīṅkaḷ enta ūr?
examples.en: I'm fine, thank you. Which town are you from?

mistakes: Do not use informal நீ (nī) automatically with an elder or stranger.

dialogue.t: வணக்கம்! நான் கார்த்திக். நீங்கள் எப்படி இருக்கிறீர்கள்?
dialogue.r: Vaṇakkam! Nāṉ Kārttik. Nīṅkaḷ eppaḍi irukkiṟīrkaḷ?
dialogue.en: Hello! I'm Karthik. How are you?

dialogue.t: நான் நன்றாக இருக்கிறேன், நன்றி. நீங்கள் எந்த ஊர்?
dialogue.r: Nāṉ naṉṟāka irukkiṟēṉ, naṉṟi. Nīṅkaḷ enta ūr?
dialogue.en: I'm fine, thank you. Which town are you from?
I'm from Bengaluru. I'm learning Tamil.

practice.q: Translate: வணக்கம் (vaṇakkam)
Write in Tamil: How are you? (formal)
Produce the complete Tamil model: Hello! My name is Divya.
practice.answer: வணக்கம்! என் பெயர் திவ்யா. (Vaṇakkam! Eṉ peyar Divyā.)

practice.q: Choose the Tamil expression for “How are you? (familiar)”.
Say naturally in Tamil: I'm fine, thank you. Which town are you from?
practice.answer: நான் நன்றாக இருக்கிறேன், நன்றி. நீங்கள் எந்த ஊர்? (Nāṉ naṉṟāka irukkiṟēṉ, naṉṟi. Nīṅkaḷ enta ūr?)

quiz.q: What does நீங்கள் எப்படி இருக்கிறீர்கள்? (nīṅkaḷ eppaḍi irukkiṟīrkaḷ?) mean here?
quiz.why: நீங்கள் எப்படி இருக்கிறீர்கள்? (nīṅkaḷ eppaḍi irukkiṟīrkaḷ?) means “How are you? (formal).”

quiz.q: What does நீ எப்படி இருக்கிறாய்? (nī eppaḍi irukkiṟāy?) mean here?
quiz.why: நீ எப்படி இருக்கிறாய்? (nī eppaḍi irukkiṟāy?) means “How are you? (familiar).”

quiz.q: What does நான் நன்றாக இருக்கிறேன் (nāṉ naṉṟāka irukkiṟēṉ) mean here?
quiz.why: நான் நன்றாக இருக்கிறேன் (nāṉ naṉṟāka irukkiṟēṉ) means “I'm fine.”

items: வணக்கம்! என் பெயர் திவ்யா. (Vaṇakkam! Eṉ peyar Divyā.)
வணக்கம்! நான் கார்த்திக். நீங்கள் எப்படி இருக்கிறீர்கள்? (Vaṇakkam! Nāṉ Kārttik. Nīṅkaḷ eppaḍi irukkiṟīrkaḷ?)
key: Hello! I'm Karthik. How are you?

lessons.title: People and Pronouns
lessons.learn: Identify people and choose singular, plural, and respectful pronouns. Learn complete forms with romanisation before analysing suffixes.

grammar.title: Pronouns and zero copula
grammar.explain: A present identity statement often places the description after the person without a separate word for “is.”
mistakes: Do not force English “am/is/are” into every Tamil identity sentence.

dialogue.t: வணக்கம்! நான் கார்த்திக். நீங்கள் எப்படி இருக்கிறீர்கள்?
dialogue.r: Vaṇakkam! Nāṉ Kārttik. Nīṅkaḷ eppaḍi irukkiṟīrkaḷ?
dialogue.en: Hello! I'm Karthik. How are you?

dialogue.t: நான் நன்றாக இருக்கிறேன், நன்றி. நீங்கள் எந்த ஊர்?
dialogue.r: Nāṉ naṉṟāka irukkiṟēṉ, naṉṟi. Nīṅkaḷ enta ūr?
dialogue.en: I'm fine, thank you. Which town are you from?
I'm from Bengaluru. I'm learning Tamil.

practice.q: Translate: நான் (nāṉ)
Write in Tamil: we (excluding you)
Produce the complete Tamil model: I
Choose the Tamil expression for “you (formal / plural)”.
Say naturally in Tamil: you (formal)

lessons.title: Home, School, and Objects
lessons.learn: Name familiar places and objects, then locate them. Tamil attaches case endings to nouns rather than placing separate prepositions before them.

grammar.title: Location with -இல் / -ல
grammar.explain: The formal locative suffix -இல் (-il), often -ல (-la) in speech, means “in/at.”
mistakes: Do not put a Tamil location marker before the noun as English does.

dialogue.en: Listen, guests are coming this evening.
Your uncle and aunt. Tidy the room.

practice.q: Translate: புத்தகம் (puttakam)
Write in Tamil: house / home
Produce the complete Tamil model: at home
Choose the Tamil expression for “work”.
Say naturally in Tamil: from Chennai

lessons.title: Food and Polite Requests
lessons.learn: Name basic foods and request an item politely. Learn spoken service phrases as wholes and notice that the verb normally comes last.

grammar.title: Object before verb
grammar.explain: Tamil’s neutral clause order is subject–object–verb. Polite requests commonly finish with an imperative form.
mistakes: Do not keep English subject–verb–object order in a basic Tamil request.

dialogue.en: Brother, one tea please. (அண்ணே = O elder brother — the vocative everyone uses for the vendor)

practice.q: Translate: சாதம் (sātam)
Write in Tamil: uncooked rice
Produce the complete Tamil model: I am hungry
Choose the Tamil expression for “lentils / dal”.
Say naturally in Tamil: The food is tasty

lessons.title: Travel and Questions
lessons.learn: Ask where a place is and identify common transport. Question words occupy the information slot, while the predicate remains near the end.

grammar.title: Information questions
grammar.explain: Use எங்கே (eṅkē, where), என்ன (eṉṉa, what), and எவ்வளவு (evvaḷavu, how much) in the clause.
mistakes: Do not add an English-style auxiliary “do” to Tamil questions.

dialogue.en: Excuse me, where is the station?

practice.q: Translate: நிலையம் (nilaiyam)
Write in Tamil: train
Produce the complete Tamil model: Where is ...?
Choose the Tamil expression for “bus”.
Say naturally in Tamil: Stop here, please

items: ... க்கு எப்படி போக வேண்டும்? (... kku eppaḍi pōka vēṇḍum?)

lessons.title: Daily Actions
lessons.learn: Describe simple routines using common verbs. Tamil verbs encode tense and person; first learn high-frequency complete models for different speakers.

grammar.title: Present and habitual action
grammar.explain: A Tamil verb stem takes tense and person endings. Spoken Tamil may shorten forms found in formal writing.
mistakes: Do not remove the final verb ending; it carries essential tense and person information.

practice.q: Translate: சாப்பிட (sāppiḍa)
Write in Tamil: go
Produce the complete Tamil model: I don't understand
Choose the Tamil expression for “come”.
Say naturally in Tamil: Speak slowly, please

items.q: Produce in Tamil: Hello! My name is Divya.
items.answer: வணக்கம்! என் பெயர் திவ்யா. (Vaṇakkam! Eṉ peyar Divyā.)

items.q: Produce in Tamil: I am hungry

pronunciation.t: Tamil contrasts short and long vowels.
pronunciation.tip: Hold long vowels about twice as long; length can change meaning.

pronunciation.t: ழ is a distinct Tamil sound.
pronunciation.tip: Curl the tongue back gently and let the sound flow along the sides.

pronunciation.t: ள and ல are different lateral sounds.
pronunciation.tip: Use a curled tongue for ள and a forward tongue for ல.

pronunciation.t: ண and ந distinguish tongue position.
pronunciation.tip: Curl back for ண; place the tongue forward for ந.
Listen to whole words; many stops become voiced between vowels.

alphabet.title: Tamil Script Foundations
alphabet.explain: Only 31 letters — no aspirates, no separate voiced sounds. க reads ka, ga or kha depending on position: one letter, three jobs. Fewer letters to learn, more listening to do. Spoken Tamil also shortens many written forms — this course teaches the written form first and flags the street version.

counting.title: Tamil Numbers
counting.explain: Tamil counts directly — people take the word பேர் (persons):
rules: Place a number before its noun in a basic counted phrase.
Learn one to twenty as whole forms before building larger quantities.
